subject: Token velocity matrix + SLA hooks — post-demo calibration
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elena Varga <elena@fleetops.com>; FleetOps - Platform Team <platform@fleetops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Token velocity matrix + SLA hooks — post-demo calibration

Hi Elena / Platform team —

Thanks for taking the demo today. Per our walkthrough I’m sending a concise recap focused on the performance constraints we need to qualify before we can finalize the Dedicated sizing / SLA sketch. I’ve attached the workload_sample CSV and a quick latency capture we collected during the session.

Key items captured (please confirm or correct):
- Typical steady-state QPS: ~6 qps (90% of daytime minutes)
- Average tokens per request: 420 tokens (median ~380, 95th ~1,200)
- Peak windows: 12:00–12:15 daily burst with short spikes up to ~85 qps (10x steady); sustained peak windows observed during promotions up to 20 minutes
- Streaming sessions: ~40 concurrent streaming connections during peak; each session averages 1–3 tokens/sec while interactive
- Latency targets: your product team asked for end-to-end first-token latency <= 250ms p95 and per-token streaming latency <= 120ms p99 for interactive workflows
- Expected growth: ~25% month-over-month for the next 3 months during the pilot phase

Preliminary implications we discussed:
- For the steady-state profile we can use a small Dedicated pool (lower-cost quantized model) with autoscale headroom for 2–3x short bursts; however sustained 20-minute peaks will require autoscale to larger nodes or routing to Hosted fallback to maintain the latency SLOs.
- Streaming latency target (120ms p99) is aggressive; will need a streaming-optimized variant and pinned model placement near users (regional routing)

Open questions / asks for FleetOps (please reply inline):
1) Can you confirm the 95th-token size is reliably below 1.5k tokens or do you have larger outliers we should plan for?
2) For the promotion window examples, are those calendar-driven (known in advance) or ad-hoc bursts? If calendar-driven we can pre-warm capacity.
3) Are any of the streaming sessions bi-directional with user tokens interleaving every 100–200ms? That increases concurrency pressure on KV cache significantly.

Next steps (proposed):
- FleetOps to confirm Q1–Q3 above and drop a sanitized sample of 48 hours (CSV) — action: FleetOps / Elena — due: 2028-06-27
- Redwood to produce a token-velocity matrix mapping (steady vs peak) to instance sizing + fallback plan — action: Sean / Marissa — draft due: 2028-06-28 (attached sketch will be updated)
- Joint call to validate SLA knobs and pre-warm plan — propose: 2028-06-29 10:00am PT — please confirm

Attachments: fleetops_workload_sample.csv (sample), latency_capture_6-24.json (demo capture), proposal-sketch.pdf (rough sizing notes)

Thanks — concise answers to the three asks will let us lock an initial sizing and a pilot SLA.

—
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Token velocity matrix + SLA hooks — post-demo calibration

On 2028-06-25 at 15:08, Sean Gallagher wrote:
> Key items captured (please confirm or correct):

Quick clarifications from our side before we build sizing:
- Treat the 95th token size as 1.5k for the first-pass sizing (we'll add headroom if FleetOps sees heavier tails)
- For QPS translation: baseline 6 qps maps to ~2.5k tokens/sec steady; 85 qps peak -> ~35k tokens/sec peak (using fleet average)
- Streaming concurrency note: if sessions interact at <200ms inter-token intervals, we should assume 2x memory overhead for KV cache per connection.

I’ll take point on the sizing matrix draft and include two flavors: streaming-optimized (lower-latency, higher-cost) and batch-optimized (more cost-efficient for non-real-time endpoints).

Marissa
Principal Product Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Varga <elena@fleetops.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@fleetops.com>, FleetOps - Platform Team <platform@fleetops.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Token velocity matrix + SLA hooks — post-demo calibration

Thanks Sean — rapid answers below inline: 

1) 95th token size: confirmed, 95th ~1.4k tokens. We have outliers up to ~3k but those are from batch exports not interactive users. You can ignore batch-export spikes for interactive SLA sizing.
2) Promotion windows: they are mostly calendar-driven (marketing campaign schedules). We can provide a schedule for the next 60 days once legal redacts customer PII. So pre-warming is possible and preferred.
3) Streaming behavior: interactive sessions are user-driven; median inter-token interval is ~300–400ms, but power-users can be ~120–150ms. We estimate ~10% of sessions are sub-200ms.

Additional data points:
- Typical session length (streaming): 20–90 seconds
- Ratio of interactive to batch requests during peak: 3:1

Action: I’ll upload a sanitized 72-hour sample to the Drive link and flag the campaign windows. ETA: 2028-06-27 EOD.

—
Elena Varga
Director, Platform Engineering | FleetOps
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elena Varga <elena@fleetops.com>, FleetOps - Platform Team <platform@fleetops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-26T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Token velocity matrix + SLA hooks — post-demo calibration

Perfect — thanks for the quick confirmations, Elena. Notes and immediate next steps based on your replies: 

- We'll size around 1.5k tokens at 95th for interactive endpoints and treat 3k+ exports as a separate batch flow (different model routing).
- Because campaign windows are calendar driven we’ll propose a pre-warm playbook (cron-based scaling + warmed reserved nodes) to avoid cold-start latency for the 12:00 bursts.
- For streaming: we’ll plan capacity assuming 10% sub-200ms sessions and include KV-cache 2x overhead headroom in the streaming-optimized flavor.

Deliverables & owners: 
- Sizing matrix (steady/peak) + cost delta (streaming vs batch flavor) — Marissa — draft 2028-06-28
- Pre-warm playbook (runbook + cron examples) — Jonas — draft 2028-06-28
- Final pilot SLA sketch and fallback policy (Hosted fallback behavior) — Sean — draft 2028-06-29

Proposed follow-up call: 2028-06-29 10:00am PT (30m). If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

If FleetOps uploads the sanitized sample we’ll run a quick token-velocity pass and confirm final sizing before the call.

Thanks —
Sean
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
